scope: Ancient Africa and Arabia priority following methodology reset
cases: Pre-Islamic South Arabia — recurrent slavery/captive enslavement in first-millennium epigraphic corpus
Punic Carthage — institutional slavery and agricultural slave labour
Aksum — recurrent slavery with bounded royal-inscription evidence for captive-taking and deportation
Late Period Egypt — pre-Ptolemaic chattel slavery evidenced through hereditary status, alienability and ownership branding
unresolved_issues: South Arabia is intentionally a multi-polity regional synthesis with unresolved geometry; it must not be rendered as one timeless polity polygon.
The South Arabian term ʿbd is semantically context-dependent; the claim relies on explicit ownership, sale and captive evidence and does not classify every ʿbd as enslaved.
Punic Carthage needs time-bounded historical geometry before publication.

Aksum is classified P2 from specialist synthesis plus bounded captive-taking evidence, but Adulis trade references are not used mechanically as territorial-practice evidence and captive status is not automatically treated as chattel slavery.
Aksum needs time-bounded historical geometry before publication; modern Ethiopia/Eritrea boundaries and maximum-extent empire maps are not acceptable substitutes.

Kush/Meroe remains a candidate rather than a claim: current review found strong warnings in specialist scholarship against assuming an ancient Middle Nile external slave trade without tighter evidence.

Late Period Egypt is P3 for institution-defining chattel practices, not P4: the specialist literature emphasizes scant documentation and a material difference from larger-scale Ptolemaic commercialization.
Late Period Egypt needs narrower time-bounded historical geometry before publication; modern Egypt is not an acceptable proxy for the full 664–330 BCE slice.

Opone has strong first-century evidence for slave export to Egypt, but a trade-node attestation does not establish territorial prevalence, captives' origins, or local status institutions; no P-level is assigned from trade alone.
No claim in this batch is part of a public release.
negative_or_deferred_candidates: Kush/Meroe — do not infer an ancient external slave trade from later Middle Nile patterns; require bounded status/captive evidence.

Garamantes — reviewed scholarship supports trans-Saharan connectivity, but slaves remain a possible rather than securely demonstrated import in the evidence inspected so far; do not create a territorial slavery claim from trade-route inference.

Opone/northern Somali coast — Periplus sections 8 and 13 securely attest slave exports at Malao and especially Opone, but preserve this as trade evidence until the data model can represent trade/events separately or local slavery evidence is found.

Rhapta/Azania — do not generalize Opone's slave-export evidence southward; inspected scholarship identifies Rhapta as a major trade port but does not independently establish slave export or territorial slavery there.
next_research: Continue ancient African coverage beyond the Mediterranean littoral, prioritizing evidence quality over filling polygons.
Investigate Kush/Meroe only through bounded status/captive evidence rather than inherited assumptions about a timeless Nile slave trade.
Evaluate a dedicated trade/event representation so strong evidence such as Opone's first-century slave exports can be mapped without misclassifying territorial practice.
Resolve time-bounded historical geometry for Carthage, Aksum and Late Period Egypt before any are considered for publication.
Continue underrepresented ancient regions after Africa/Arabia rather than defaulting to dense Atlantic or Mediterranean archives.
